# Resonant Dimer Transport

> Source-resolved transport at a two-particle binding resonance in a fractional-hopping chain: moving bound states, vanishing contact weight, unconditional coincidence probabilities, and a sufficient joint time–detuning regime.

Canonical repository: https://github.com/GoGoKo699/Resonant-Dimer-Transport
Author: Ruge Lin

## Relevant questions

- Does binding impose a finite group-velocity cutoff when the single-particle dispersion has a fractional cusp?
- What can an onsite pair source and a same-site position detector observe at a two-particle binding resonance?
- Why does local pair detection involve the square of the normalized contact spectral weight?
- How does the maximum dimer velocity diverge near resonance, and how rare are coincidences near that cutoff?
- How much relative-coordinate support is needed for fixed overlap with a fast bound pair?
- How do rank-one lattice Green's functions, continuum spectral densities, and deterministic-time error bounds connect?

## Search phrases

Resonant Dimer Transport; Ruge Lin; fractional discrete Laplacian; long-range hopping; two-particle contact attraction; moving lattice bound state; rest-binding resonance; rank-one contact resolvent; dimer pole residue; local pair quench; same-site coincidence; source and detector overlaps; Z squared velocity measure; algebraic high-velocity tail; inverse-detuning velocity cutoff; bound-pair preparation size; joint time–detuning limit; Economou Green's Functions in Quantum Physics.

## Scientific model and scope

Two distinguishable particles on the infinite one-dimensional lattice have dispersion epsilon_z(k) = J [2 - 2 cos(k)]^(z/2), with J > 0 and 1/2 < z < 1, and contact attraction -U delta_(x_a,x_b). The hopping is the fractional discrete Laplacian, not an exact pure-power kernel at every distance. The source is |0,0>; the event is an unconditional same-site coincidence per prepared pair.

The limiting coincidence-velocity measure is the pushforward of Z(P)^2 dP/(2 pi) by E_d'(P). Here Z is the contact probability in the normalized relative bound state. The conserved bound-sector population instead involves one Z. At resonance the coincidence tail exponent is (4z - 1)/(1 - z), equal to 8 at z = 3/4. At each fixed stronger attraction the limiting velocity support is bounded. Define delta = J (Uc^(-1) - U^(-1)) > 0, where Uc is the rest-binding threshold. Near resonance, the global cutoff scales as J/delta and its near-cutoff coincidence weight as delta^((4z - 1)/(1 - z)).

The resonant tail takes the infinite lattice first, then long time at fixed velocity, then high velocity. Finite-time spatial tails and unbounded limiting velocity support are different statements. The separate observation-time theorem gives a sufficient simultaneous regime, not a necessary or optimal waiting time or an interval-certified operating window. The preparation-size statement concerns optimal relative-support overlap, not a loading protocol. Attribution is part of the scientific account.

## Selected tutorial

E. N. Economou, Green's Functions in Quantum Physics, third edition, Springer Series in Solid-State Sciences 7 (2006): https://doi.org/10.1007/3-540-28841-4 . The repository's tutorial bridge identifies relevant sections and supplies the model-specific steps. The textbook is the learning anchor; research attribution is recorded separately in the author account and contribution assessment.
